DIESEL SKIMMING 2019

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We go undercover to crack an illegal Diesel Skimming operation on the East Rand in Joburg.

Summary:
While we all know that transport costs has skyrocketed as fuel prices steadily climb – with yet another increase early September, but you might be surprised to find out that, that’s not the only reason for increases...

We uncover an illegal operation that is fuelling transport costs hikes...It’s called Diesel Skimming - hundreds of drivers from around the country are making unscheduled pit stops to siphon off litres and litres of fuel in exchange for cash.

Carte Blanche teams up with a local investigator to catch the culprits red handed and crack the syndicate.


Further information:
Investigator Jakes Muller has been exposing diesel skimming syndicates for the last decade. He identifies suspicious operations and sets up a series of hidden cameras capturing the crooks on the job. He has endless videos of drivers selling off their employers fuel to illegal operations at these unscheduled pit stops from fields to plots in built up industrial areas.

WHAT WILL WE SEE
Anything between 9 and 17 trucks a day – day and night – pull in to a dodgy looking yard where the drivers siphon off between 25 – 200 litres of diesel. They get paid R200 cash per 25 litre drum – that’s R8 a litre, much cheaper than the standard garage rates of R14.37 per litre. It’s cash the drivers pocket at the expense of the transport company they work for.

You can clearly see the trucks’ registration numbers as they drive in. Then you see them arriving with empty drums, taking the diesel and walking away with full drums. So it will be easy to identify the transport company being ripped off.

WHO IS BEHIND IT?
In most of the cases Jakes has handled the operation is run by foreigners. The fuel is decanted to bigger drums which transported off site – often the fuel gets offered to dodgy garages at below market prices or directly to unscrupulous transporters who buy black market fuel.

OUR SITE
In this current case the fuel is transported to house nearby – we are busy getting surveillance done to establish exactly what the MO is.

WHAT IS BEING DONE?
Once the transport companies have been alerted the drivers are usually dismissed and charges are laid against them as well as the buyers of the siphoned diesel. But when arrests linked to the diesel skimming operations are made the suspects often get bail and head out of the country resulting in the cases being thrown out eventually. On the rare occasions when the cases go to trial the sentencing isn’t very severe with fines as little as R500. The illegal operation costs the transport industry hundreds of thousands of rands.

EXPERT – THE ROAD FREIGHT ASSOCIATION
85% of consumer goods transported by road – these losses make it to the end user.
We speak to Gavin Kelly from The Road Freight Association about the bigger picture. While it may be 25 litres here and 50 litres there, eventually these losses work their way into the transport costs that will end up being covered by consumers down the line. It’s estimated that the average truck loses around R35 000 per year just in stolen diesel.

AFFECTED TRANSPORTER – THE LITTLE GUY
Bradely Naidoo runs a small transport company with 15 trucks – his drivers have been caught by Jakes more than once – he’s willing to loan us a truck and a driver to do a sting - capturing how the operation works up close on hidden camera.

THE BIGGER GUYS JUST DON’T SEEM TO CARE – SUPERGROUP
Supergroup Trucks are regulars in Jakes’ videos – but they don’t care and don’t take action. They hire out trucks, so technically it’s their clients losing the money on diesel. BUT, it’s Supergroup drivers doing the dodgy deals. Essentially they are supporting crime through their in action while their clients pay the price.

BUST
We get police to assist with a raid on the site. We’ll also go to the site where the diesel gets transported to.

TANK OF DIESEL THAT WILL SKIMMED & UNDERCOVER OPERATIVE THAT WILL ACCOMPANY DRIVER.

FINAL SCRIPT DIESEL SKIMMING 2019

VO: It’s called Diesel Skimming. Truck drivers make unscheduled pit stops to siphon off litres and litres of fuel in exchange for hard cash.

LINK: It’s not a new trend , but it happens every single day around the country. The process is simple, but it’s one that costs transport industry big bucks. With drivers pocketing the cash while the transporters foot the bill for the losses.

JAKES: // It's been going on for years and nobody's doing something about it. // // They killing the companies with diesel theft

VO: Private Investigator Jakes Muller is a master at exposing diesel skimming operations, using hidden cameras to catch the crooks on the job.

It’s easy, it’s quick and the money is good for the dodgy truckers.

JAKES: Two three minutes and they fill it // all sorts of trucks big ones, smalls ones, horse and trailers – everything comes there.

VO: The process isn’t rocket science.

Watch carefully… using a hosepipe and a 25 litre drum – the skimmers simply connect the pipe to the fuel tank and feed the other end of the pipe into the drum – and that’s it – the driver sells off diesel that belongs to the truck owner.

JAKES: Sometimes we get eight to 10 trucks a day. And they taking out some of them two drums there's five drums there's nine drums // during their day at night. 24 hours they are doing it 24/7.

VO: The Road Freight Association of South Africa represents over 700 transport companies moving roughly 85% of all goods in the country by road. Diesel skimming has a massive impact on the industry explains CEO Gavin Kelly.

GAVIN: // the cost of transport is based on the operation of the vehicle. And one of the biggest cost factors is diesel usage.

VO: At the end of the day consumers will pick up the tab for these losses when the prices of goods go up at the tills – because transport costs make up close to 12% of the final price.

GAVIN: in terms of the total number of litres sold and we're looking at probably about a billion litres in terms of of land transport. And if you skimming of one per cent of it that's a lot of fuel




VO: The illegal skimming usually happens in industrial areas, close to a main road, ensuring easy access for the trucks.

JAKES: // everywhere there where there's trucks going there's an opportunity for them to do this.
DEREK: How do the drivers get involved.
JAKES: These guys are buying the diesel from them. They stand next to that road and they show the drivers. That they must come and Sell the diesel.

VO: This clip is from a skimming site in Isando, on Johannesburg’s East Rand. The driver selling off his boss’ diesel - works for Merc-Man Transport in Vanderbijl Park. In total he siphoned off 9 drums in one shot.

We showed the footage to Alex Ferreira, the operations manager.

ALEX: // I can't I can't believe it. // so many drums - and out of one vehicle. That's about 200 litres right there.
DEREK: How do you feel when you see this.
ALEX: Oh I feel very betrayed // This can totally sink the company

LINK: Now there are devices on the market to prevent the siphoning of fuel – but where there is a will there is a way and the scamsters soon enough find their away around it.

JAKES: // they take the drain black out underneath the tank where they loosen the pipe On their return and let the truck idle and then pull it out there. They always find a way to do it.

VO: But diesel skimming often also goes undetected because there are so many variables when it comes to fuel consumption – Ferreira says after months of fuel usage discrepancies they had their suspicions.

ALEX: // your diesel ratio should be about a third of your expenses of your income. //. And now where we are at this stage and this is reality. It's almost half now. So you can imagine the theft that's going on

VO: Curious to find out just how easy it really is, we sent in an undercover crew posing as a dodgy trucker and his assistant. But it seems the skimmers were weary at first explains our operative.

OPERATIVE: // I think the guys wanted to see if we were really serious about selling the diesel, so they took a while before the approached us.

VO: After a brief chat, they struck a deal and the culprits came running with 25 litres drums to siphon off the diesel. It seems that skimmers welcome all new business.

OPERATIVE: We told them we wanted to sell four drums and they gave us the price per drum – which it was R200 per drum //
DEREK: This is it.
OPERATIOVE: They gave me R800 rands… //
DEREK: not bad for a little morning’s work if you are a truck driver –
OPERATIVE: not bad at all….. yes.

VO: That works out to R8 a litre, at less than half the petrol station retail price of about R16 - it’s a profitable business.

GAVIN: // it's really about getting fuel that you're not paying for and selling on. So if I get a litre of fuel free in inverted commas and I sell it for Rand I'm making a rand profit// there's a market for it it's not like trying to flog a huge expensive car that you've got a very very small market. Everybody needs fuel

VO: At the Isando site, the operation is so busy – they even have drivers who come to collect the full drums and move it off site.

It’s clear, this operation is organised.

OPERATIVE: // they are not just there but taking chances, they are there, they are organised, they know that anything can happen at anytime, that’s why they hide there stuff – if you go there without knowing you will never know those guys are buying diesel from truck drivers.

VO: Kelly says more often than not there are syndicates involved.

DEREK: Gavin is it's Syndicates or is it just random fraudsters.
GAVIN: It's not just // Mickey Mouse …… // they're definitely very big players and syndicates involved // We know of depots around Gauteng

VO: Looking at the footage, although the criminality is blatant, arrests, are a scarcity.

DEREK: the guys siphpining don’t get brought to book
JAKES: No not really, no one gets inovlved there - that’s the problem.

VO: Diesel doesn’t have identifying markers, so it is difficult to link the culprits to the crime, unless you catch them red handed. So we sent in a second sting truck.

For the bust, we were joined by the police’s specific crimes unit. After a quick briefing, we moved into position, closer to the site. We’re hoping to catch them in the act.

LINK: It’s amazing how open this site is – middle of houses, shops, // the site is just to my right here, we’ve got one police unit here and one on the other side – the idea is to sandwich them.

DEREK UPSOUND: Waiting for your signal, Then we’re ready to move in.

COP: Trek die pyp uit…
DEREK: There’s the evidence just there

VO: We scouted around the site to see where the diesel had been hidden.

DEREK UPSOUND: Yah, drums here, these are full, check -// that’s how full it is – yah all of these are full…

VO: It’s highly likely that the diesel is intended for the black market, according to Kelly.

GAVIN: // There is a fair amount of it going cross-border but there's a lot of domestic market for that. And if I can buy the fuel //for five six Rand less than we should buy at the pump. There Is a huge market for it.

VO: With four of the foot soldiers in hand cuffs, it was time to look for the king pin. We had details of storage site not far from where the diesel gets siphoned.

LINK: Once of the drums are filled, they are put in the back of a bakkie and brought to this house in the East, we’re about to follow the police in here now.

RUNNING IN….
UPSOUND DEREK: Jeeze look at this, is this an operation or what?

VO: The house is barely furnished. Inside were three men that the cops pulled out for questioning.

LINK: Look at the size of this operation, and it’s in the middle of suburbia, surrounded by other houses.

VO: After being cuffed and questioned. One of the suspects was quick to spill the beans to deflect attention from himself, denying any involvement.

SUSPECT: This thing is for Bheki M1 // He is a Zimbabwean guy, he is operating with this stuff //
DEREK: So you’re not invovled?
SUSPECT: …. Not involved.

VO: According to the suspect, the person in charge of the house is a man called Johan and he’s apparently close by visiting a friend. The police apprehended him immediately as we arrived.

DEREK: who’s the leader of the operation?
JOHAN: basically I know a guy called, his name is Bheki, he’s the one who is operating.
DEREK: Last firday you were involved
JOHAN: I was not involved in nothing – I promise you sir…

VO: But that’s not true according, Private Investigator Jakes, Johan has been placed at the scene.

JAKES: //last week Friday he helped them off load the diesel by the house.
DEREK: are you sure?
JAKES: sure. //
DEREK: do you admit you’ve been at the sites?
JOHAN: I go there but I don’t steal, the guys just tells me to load the drums.

VO: With all fingers pointing to Bheki, we were taken to the house where he lives, also in the area. The staff let us in while the police searched the property.

LINK: So diesel pipes in the store room, staff here, but no sign of bheki, he left on foot for now leave it to cops and courts.

VO: Back at the storage house, the police identified one of Bheki’s alleged buyers, Shaun. On his phone there were these messages – discussing an order for 5000 litres with Bheki.

UPSOUND WHATSAPPS AUDIO
SHAUN: Do you have the diesel, what’s the story, the guys are asking?
BHEKI: now I don’t have, I only have 500 litres

DEREK: Can you tell your side of the story here – we’ve seen everything on your phone, we know who you buy from
SHAUN: I don’t deal with diesel
DEREK: But that’s your phone.
DEREK: how much do you sell it for?
SHAUN:I didn’t sell it, I enquired, to sell it and make the extra bucks but nothing materialised…. Different case if bought the diesel but I didn’t buy it

VO: With still no sign of Bheki, the alleged kingpin, we decided called him. But first we were going to ask about a new order…

DEREK: Have you got 5000 l of diesel?
BHEKI: you want diesel – how many do you want?
DEREK: 5000 l
BHEKI: Aaah, nothing, I’m not dealing with diesel any more
DEREK: It’s CB here – the MNET programme, story on diesel skimming and all fingers are being pointed at you Bheki – we’re at the house where you store it…
BHEKI: I don’t deal with stolen diesel – people suspect that I deal with stolen diesel
DEREK: how about we meet and you can explain yourself
BHEKI: don’t just arrest me
DEREK: We won’t arrest you but the police might

VO: Bheki agreed to meet us, but obviously never showed up.
Jakes says until the whole gang is behind bars, the police will have their work cut out for them.

JAKES: You catch them here today, tomorrow they open a kilometer away and they open again.

ALEX: //it's an ongoing struggle. You constantly try to battle this thing of corruption and crime
DEREK: but it's also a losing battle.
ALEX: It's a losing battle at this stage

ALEX: // your diesel ratio should be about a third of your expenses of your income. //. And now where we are at this stage and this is reality. It's almost half now. So you can imagine the theft that's going on VO: Curious to find out just how easy it really is, we sent in an undercover crew posing as a dodgy trucker and his assistant. But it seems the skimmers were weary at first explains our operative. OPERATIVE: // I think the guys wanted to see if we were really serious about selling the diesel, so they took a while before the approached us. VO: After a brief chat, they struck a deal and the culprits came running with 25 litres drums to siphon off the diesel. It seems that skimmers welcome all new business. OPERATIVE: We told them we wanted to sell four drums and they gave us the price per drum – which it was R200 per drum // DEREK: This is it. OPERATIOVE: They gave me R800 rands… // DEREK: not bad for a little morning’s work if you are a truck driver – OPERATIVE: not bad at all….. yes. VO: That works out to R8 a litre, at less than half the petrol station retail price of about R16 - it’s a profitable business. GAVIN: // it's really about getting fuel that you're not paying for and selling on. So if I get a litre of fuel free in inverted commas and I sell it for Rand I'm making a rand profit// there's a market for it it's not like trying to flog a huge expensive car that you've got a very very small market. Everybody needs fuel VO: At the Isando site, the operation is so busy – they even have drivers who come to collect the full drums and move it off site. It’s clear, this operation is organised. OPERATIVE: // they are not just there but taking chances, they are there, they are organised, they know that anything can happen at anytime, that’s why they hide there stuff – if you go there without knowing you will never know those guys are buying diesel from truck drivers. VO: Kelly says more often than not there are syndicates involved. DEREK: Gavin is it's Syndicates or is it just random fraudsters. GAVIN: It's not just // Mickey Mouse …… // they're definitely very big players and syndicates involved // We know of depots around Gauteng VO: Looking at the footage, although the criminality is blatant, arrests, are a scarcity. DEREK: the guys siphpining don’t get brought to book JAKES: No not really, no one gets inovlved there - that’s the problem. VO: Diesel doesn’t have identifying markers, so it is difficult to link the culprits to the crime, unless you catch them red handed. So we sent in a second sting truck. For the bust, we were joined by the police’s specific crimes unit. After a quick briefing, we moved into position, closer to the site. We’re hoping to catch them in the act. LINK: It’s amazing how open this site is – middle of houses, shops, // the site is just to my right here, we’ve got one police unit here and one on the other side – the idea is to sandwich them. DEREK UPSOUND: Waiting for your signal, Then we’re ready to move in. COP: Trek die pyp uit… DEREK: There’s the evidence just there VO: We scouted around the site to see where the diesel had been hidden. DEREK UPSOUND: Yah, drums here, these are full, check -// that’s how full it is – yah all of these are full… VO: It’s highly likely that the diesel is intended for the black market, according to Kelly. GAVIN: // There is a fair amount of it going cross-border but there's a lot of domestic market for that. And if I can buy the fuel //for five six Rand less than we should buy at the pump. There Is a huge market for it. VO: With four of the foot soldiers in hand cuffs, it was time to look for the king pin. We had details of storage site not far from where the diesel gets siphoned. LINK: Once of the drums are filled, they are put in the back of a bakkie and brought to this house in the East, we’re about to follow the police in here now. RUNNING IN…. UPSOUND DEREK: Jeeze look at this, is this an operation or what? VO: The house is barely furnished. Inside were three men that the cops pulled out for questioning. LINK: Look at the size of this operation, and it’s in the middle of suburbia, surrounded by other houses. VO: After being cuffed and questioned. One of the suspects was quick to spill the beans to deflect attention from himself, denying any involvement. SUSPECT: This thing is for Bheki M1 // He is a Zimbabwean guy, he is operating with this stuff // DEREK: So you’re not invovled? SUSPECT: …. Not involved. VO: According to the suspect, the person in charge of the house is a man called Johan and he’s apparently close by visiting a friend. The police apprehended him immediately as we arrived. DEREK: who’s the leader of the operation? JOHAN: basically I know a guy called, his name is Bheki, he’s the one who is operating. DEREK: Last firday you were involved JOHAN: I was not involved in nothing – I promise you sir… VO: But that’s not true according, Private Investigator Jakes, Johan has been placed at the scene. JAKES: //last week Friday he helped them off load the diesel by the house. DEREK: are you sure? JAKES: sure. // DEREK: do you admit you’ve been at the sites? JOHAN: I go there but I don’t steal, the guys just tells me to load the drums. VO: With all fingers pointing to Bheki, we were taken to the house where he lives, also in the area. The staff let us in while the police searched the property. LINK: So diesel pipes in the store room, staff here, but no sign of bheki, he left on foot for now leave it to cops and courts. VO: Back at the storage house, the police identified one of Bheki’s alleged buyers, Shaun. On his phone there were these messages – discussing an order for 5000 litres with Bheki. UPSOUND WHATSAPPS AUDIO SHAUN: Do you have the diesel, what’s the story, the guys are asking? BHEKI: now I don’t have, I only have 500 litres DEREK: Can you tell your side of the story here – we’ve seen everything on your phone, we know who you buy from SHAUN: I don’t deal with diesel DEREK: But that’s your phone. DEREK: how much do you sell it for? SHAUN:I didn’t sell it, I enquired, to sell it and make the extra bucks but nothing materialised…. Different case if bought the diesel but I didn’t buy it VO: With still no sign of Bheki, the alleged kingpin, we decided called him. But first we were going to ask about a new order… DEREK: Have you got 5000 l of diesel? BHEKI: you want diesel – how many do you want? DEREK: 5000 l BHEKI: Aaah, nothing, I’m not dealing with diesel any more DEREK: It’s CB here – the MNET programme, story on diesel skimming and all fingers are being pointed at you Bheki – we’re at the house where you store it… BHEKI: I don’t deal with stolen diesel – people suspect that I deal with stolen diesel DEREK: how about we meet and you can explain yourself BHEKI: don’t just arrest me DEREK: We won’t arrest you but the police might VO: Bheki agreed to meet us, but obviously never showed up. Jakes says until the whole gang is behind bars, the police will have their work cut out for them. JAKES: You catch them here today, tomorrow they open a kilometer away and they open again. ALEX: //it's an ongoing struggle. You constantly try to battle this thing of corruption and crime DEREK: but it's also a losing battle. ALEX: It's a losing battle at this stage PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: We go undercover to crack an illegal Diesel Skimming operation on the East Rand on Joburg – where litres and litres of fuel get siphoned off for hard cash. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We go undercover to crack an illegal Diesel Skimming operation on the East Rand in Joburg.
metadata.Summary: While we all know that transport costs has skyrocketed as fuel prices steadily climb – with yet another increase early September, but you might be surprised to find out that, that’s not the only reason for increases... We uncover an illegal operation that is fuelling transport costs hikes...It’s called Diesel Skimming - hundreds of drivers from around the country are making unscheduled pit stops to siphon off litres and litres of fuel in exchange for cash. Carte Blanche teams up with a local investigator to catch the culprits red handed and crack the syndicate.
metadata.Further information: Investigator Jakes Muller has been exposing diesel skimming syndicates for the last decade. He identifies suspicious operations and sets up a series of hidden cameras capturing the crooks on the job. He has endless videos of drivers selling off their employers fuel to illegal operations at these unscheduled pit stops from fields to plots in built up industrial areas. WHAT WILL WE SEE Anything between 9 and 17 trucks a day – day and night – pull in to a dodgy looking yard where the drivers siphon off between 25 – 200 litres of diesel. They get paid R200 cash per 25 litre drum – that’s R8 a litre, much cheaper than the standard garage rates of R14.37 per litre. It’s cash the drivers pocket at the expense of the transport company they work for. You can clearly see the trucks’ registration numbers as they drive in. Then you see them arriving with empty drums, taking the diesel and walking away with full drums. So it will be easy to identify the transport company being ripped off. WHO IS BEHIND IT? In most of the cases Jakes has handled the operation is run by foreigners. The fuel is decanted to bigger drums which transported off site – often the fuel gets offered to dodgy garages at below market prices or directly to unscrupulous transporters who buy black market fuel. OUR SITE In this current case the fuel is transported to house nearby – we are busy getting surveillance done to establish exactly what the MO is. WHAT IS BEING DONE? Once the transport companies have been alerted the drivers are usually dismissed and charges are laid against them as well as the buyers of the siphoned diesel. But when arrests linked to the diesel skimming operations are made the suspects often get bail and head out of the country resulting in the cases being thrown out eventually. On the rare occasions when the cases go to trial the sentencing isn’t very severe with fines as little as R500. The illegal operation costs the transport industry hundreds of thousands of rands. EXPERT – THE ROAD FREIGHT ASSOCIATION 85% of consumer goods transported by road – these losses make it to the end user. We speak to Gavin Kelly from The Road Freight Association about the bigger picture. While it may be 25 litres here and 50 litres there, eventually these losses work their way into the transport costs that will end up being covered by consumers down the line. It’s estimated that the average truck loses around R35 000 per year just in stolen diesel. AFFECTED TRANSPORTER – THE LITTLE GUY Bradely Naidoo runs a small transport company with 15 trucks – his drivers have been caught by Jakes more than once – he’s willing to loan us a truck and a driver to do a sting - capturing how the operation works up close on hidden camera. THE BIGGER GUYS JUST DON’T SEEM TO CARE – SUPERGROUP Supergroup Trucks are regulars in Jakes’ videos – but they don’t care and don’t take action. They hire out trucks, so technically it’s their clients losing the money on diesel. BUT, it’s Supergroup drivers doing the dodgy deals. Essentially they are supporting crime through their in action while their clients pay the price. BUST We get police to assist with a raid on the site. We’ll also go to the site where the diesel gets transported to. EXTRA COSTS TANK OF DIESEL THAT WILL SKIMMED & UNDERCOVER OPERATIVE THAT WILL ACCOMPANY DRIVER.
